elements.element: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause states: “This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York.”

elements.element: The designated courts are the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause designates “the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.”

elements.element: Jurisdiction of the designated New York County courts is exclusive for all disputes under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Although the clause generally provides for exclusive jurisdiction, it permits either party to seek temporary injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction. The preferred position contains no such exception, so jurisdiction is not exclusive for all disputes.

elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not any permitted fallback law.

elements.element: The designated courts correspond to the selected fallback law: Delaware courts for Delaware law, California courts for California law, or the courts of London for the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause designates courts in New York County rather than Delaware courts, California courts, or the courts of London.

result.reason: The New York governing-law and forum designations match the preferred position, but the added temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out permits proceedings outside New York County and therefore defeats the required exclusive jurisdiction. The carve-out was unnecessary to implement either stated position, so the redline is not minimal. The clause is otherwise coherent and does not disturb unrelated terms, although describing the jurisdiction as “exclusive” while adding a broad forum exception reduces precision.
